data.title: PM Modi to inaugurate RBI data centre in Bhubaneswar, garment facility in Varanasi on October 25
data.description:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on Sunday, October 25, to inaugurate a garment manufacturing unit in Varanasi, attend an Indian Air Force aerial display along the Ganges and open the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, according to an official press release.

Modi's engagements will begin at around 11 am in Varanasi, where he will inaugurate Arvind Limited's newly established garment manufacturing facility. The unit is expected to boost the textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystem, encourage industrial expansion and generate employment, particularly for women.

The facility will adopt modern manufacturing practices and cater to a global customer base, enabling garments produced in Varanasi to reach international markets, the release stated. The project is also expected to reinforce Uttar Pradesh's position as an industrial investment destination and support manufacturing-driven economic growth.

The initiative, which will predominantly involve women, also reflects the emphasis on women-led development, according to the release.

IAF aerial display at Namo Ghat

At around 1 pm, the Prime Minister will attend the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi as the chief guest. The event, organised to mark the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force (IAF), will be held under the theme "Wings over Ganges".

The display will feature several combat aircraft, including the Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, SU-30MKI and Rafale, alongside transport aircraft. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army will also take part, highlighting jointness in military operations.

The IAF's leading display formations, including the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team and the Sarang Helicopter Display Team, will demonstrate precision flying, coordination and operational excellence during the programme, the press release said.

Following his engagements in Uttar Pradesh, Modi will travel to Odisha for the inauguration of the RBI's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar at approximately 4.45 pm. He will also address the gathering.

RBI data centre to strengthen financial infrastructure

The newly developed facilities are intended to enhance the technological infrastructure supporting India's financial system by establishing a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing environment for the RBI and the wider financial sector.

The complex will house four advanced data centres to accommodate critical payment and settlement systems, as well as other flagship initiatives. It has received Tier IV certification from the Uptime Institute, a global benchmark for data centre infrastructure, placing it in the highest category of operational resilience.

According to the release, the facility ranks among the world's largest Tier IV-certified installations in the Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) sector.

The infrastructure is expected to improve the accessibility, efficiency and dependability of digital financial services while providing a secure technological base for India's increasingly digital financial economy. It is also expected to strengthen the RBI's standing in digital infrastructure among central banks.

The accompanying Cybersecurity Training Institute will offer specialised training, research and capability-building programmes in cybersecurity and enterprise technology for the financial sector.

Its focus areas will include emerging and advanced technologies relevant to the BFSI industry, such as quantum computing and artificial intelligence, the release added.

data.title: Hyperliquid Strategies Expands PURR Stock Buyback As HYPE Extends Monthly Losses
data.description:
Key points:
  • Hyperliquid’s token edged lower on Saturday, a day after Hyperliquid Strategies more than tripled its stock buyback program to $100 million.
  • PURR stock closed up over 1% on Friday, while HYPE has fallen over 19% in the past month.
  • CME Group CEO Terry Duffy raised concerns about Hyperliquid’s lack of know-your-customer checks and the risks of automatic liquidations.

Hyperliquid (HYPE) edged lower on Saturday, even after its treasury company, Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR), more than tripled its stock buyback program to $100 million.

Hyperliquid Strategies said on Friday that its board approved raising its stock repurchase program from $30 million to up to $100 million. About $72 million remained available under the expanded authorization, which meant that the company had already used roughly $28 million. The program's end date also moved from December 5, 2026, to October 31, 2027.

The company said the increase reflected the “Board's confidence in the Company's long-term capital strategy." Hyperliquid Strategies is "currently the largest HYPE-focused digital asset treasury vehicle." Among the risks it listed in its announcement, it said its stock price "will be highly correlated to the price of HYPE tokens."

HYPE Slides As PURR Stock Gains

Hyperliquid Strategies held about 38.8 million HYPE tokens, worth roughly $2.9 billion, according to its treasury dashboard.

PURR stock closed up over 1% on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around PURR was also in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

In contrast, HYPE’s price was down over 2% over the past 24 hours. Over the past month, HYPE has fallen over 19%, posting a stark contrast from last month, when HYPE posted an all-time high of $97.96, over a month ago. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around HYPE remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

However, HYPE was up over 197% so far this year.

CME CEO Raises KYC Concerns

Hyperliquid also faced questions about how it would operate in the U.S. after CME Group CEO Terry Duffy said that Hyperliquid was “basically the plumbing” and that its users should carry the regulatory burden. Speaking on Bloomberg’s Odd Lots podcast on Tuesday, Duffy said, “don't know because there's no KYC. We don't know who they are. So there's a lot of violation of U.S. law for him to deploy what he was suggesting to manage” on the rival firm.

He also warned about automatic liquidations on highly leveraged products. Duffy said such positions “can cascade and create market-moving events because of the high leverage and the small amount of dollars.”

Duffy’s comments came a day before CME reported $1.7 billion in revenue, its highest for a third quarter on record. “Our average daily volume reached 29.4 million contracts, the highest Q3 ADV on record,” Duffy said. On the earnings call, he pointed to “the strong traction of our 24/7 cryptocurrency products launched earlier this year.”

data.title: Bitcoin Hashrate Reclaims One Zettahash As Mining Competition Rebounds
data.description:
TL;DR: BlocksBridge reported Bitcoin’s seven-day hashrate above one zettahash in the week to October 22. Mining competition has recovered despite companies shifting some infrastructure toward AI.

A mining company can switch strategy without making Bitcoin mining any easier for the businesses that remain. New network data puts that distinction in focus.

In its October 22 Miner Weekly report, BlocksBridge Consulting said the network’s seven-day average hashrate had recovered above one zettahash per second, its highest level since March 3. One zettahash is equivalent to 1,000 exahashes per second.

The report also recorded a 5.92% increase in mining difficulty on October 16. Together, the figures show that announcements about individual operators leaving mining cannot be treated as a direct measure of network-wide competition.

A Mining Exit Does Not Necessarily Remove The Machines

BlocksBridge’s analysis separates a site’s future use from the fate of the equipment installed there. A facility can shift toward AI infrastructure while Bitcoin mining machines are sold or relocated, allowing them to contribute computing power elsewhere.

That distinction does not establish where every additional unit of hashrate came from. It does explain why corporate announcements and network data can point in different directions without contradicting each other.

For an operator that keeps mining, the relevant competitive field is the worldwide network. A rival’s strategic exit only reduces that field if the associated computing capacity actually disappears and is not offset by activity elsewhere.

The same caution applies to expansion plans. Announced capacity, installed machines and equipment actively submitting work are different stages. Only the last contributes to observed network performance.

Hashrate, Difficulty And Revenue Measure Different Things

A hashrate figure is an estimate of computational work, not a direct meter reading from every miner. Blockchain.com’s chart methodology explains that estimates use block production and difficulty; short periods can fluctuate because finding blocks involves randomness. A seven-day average helps smooth that noise.

That is why the time window matters. The reported one-zettahash milestone refers to a seven-day average through the October 22 report, not a guaranteed reading at every moment since then or a separate 30-day measure.

Mining difficulty is the protocol’s adjustment to the work required to find a block. The Bitcoin developer documentation describes a recalculation every 2,016 blocks, targeting roughly two weeks for that interval. Faster block production generally leads to a harder target for the next period.

Revenue is another question. More network computing power does not automatically mean more income for each machine. With other conditions unchanged, an operator supplying the same amount of work faces a smaller relative share when competing capacity expands.

Profitability also depends on the value of block rewards and fees, power costs and equipment efficiency. A rise in Bitcoin hashrate therefore cannot, by itself, establish whether a miner’s margins improved.

The rebound is evidence of renewed network competition over the reported period. Its commercial significance rests on who can supply that work economically, rather than on whether a prominent company has changed its strategy.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Axon Announces Body 5: Next-Generation Camera Built for the AI Era
data.description:
Axon Body 5 delivers 25x the AI processing power of earlier-generation cameras, with upgraded connectivity, audio and battery life to support real-time situational awareness in the field

SCOTTSDALE, Ariz., Oct. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Axon (Nasdaq: AXON), the global leader in public safety technology, today announced Axon Body 5, its newest body-worn camera designed to bring more powerful intelligence, connectivity and real-time support directly to officers in the field.

For years, Axon body cameras have helped agencies capture critical evidence and create greater transparency. Body 5 is built to help officers during the call, with information, assistance and backup on the spot.

"Officers shouldn't have to choose between getting information and watching the scene. With Axon Body 5, they don't," said Rick Smith, Axon Founder and CEO. "They capture a license or document with the camera, keep their hands free and eyes up, and get information faster than writing it down and calling it in by radio. An officer fully engaged with the person in front of them, not down at a notepad, is a safer officer and a better-served community."

Axon Body 5: Built for the AI Era

Built from the ground up for the AI era, Axon Body 5 delivers 25x the AI processing power than earlier generation Axon body cameras, alongside advancements in connectivity, audio, video and battery life. Together, these upgrades give the camera the physical power to run smarter AI features — both today and as new AI tools are developed in the future — while also making it more dependable for officers to use every day.

For the first time, Axon is also introducing two versions of its latest flagship camera: Axon Body 5 and Axon Body 5 Pro.

Both models feature several key advancements, including:

  • 25x more processing power for AI: A powerful new computing architecture creates the capacity to support current and future AI features directly on the body camera.
  • Enhanced video: Improved video captures clearer evidence across challenging environments, including better low-light performance.
  • Improved connectivity: Seamless connectivity in urban and remote environments - and more precise location capability - helps officers, cameras and remote support teams stay connected when timely information matters most.
  • Longer battery life: 20% more battery life than the previous generation helps keep the camera ready and connected throughout an officer's shift.

The Axon Body 5 Pro will continue to gain new AI capabilities as they become available, growing along with the AI Era Plan. Additionally, new hardware features include:

  • A near-focus camera: An additional dedicated camera lens lets officers scan driver's licenses to check status and search for wants or warrants in seconds, without returning to the patrol vehicle, with relevant information sent to Axon Fusus to support real-time operations.
  • Front-facing speakers: Four additional speakers project even more powerful audio toward the person an officer is speaking with, helping real-time translations from Axon Assistant carry more clearly over heavy traffic or crowd noise. 
  • Additional memory: Extra space lets the camera run several AI tools at once, helping officers stay better informed and work faster.

Bringing More of Axon's AI Era Into the Field

Axon Body 5 helps officers get more out of the Axon AI Era Plan by bringing smart tools right to the scene. Axon's portfolio already supports public safety professionals across a growing range of tasks. For example, Draft One helps officers turn body-camera audio into high-quality report drafts and Axon Assistant provides voice-based information access and real-time translation.

Increasingly, Axon is also bringing AI into real-time operations.

Axon Guardian is a new category of AI features within the AI Era Plan that was specifically created to work with an officer's field-based devices - starting with body cameras and in-car cameras - to improve safety. Guardian is designed to flag potential risks as situations unfold and create alerts when additional attention may be needed. Two of the first features include:

  • Escalation Detection: When an Axon Body 4 or Axon Body 5 camera is activated and recording, Guardian has the ability to detect potential conflicts in real time and create an alert in Axon Fusus. A human reviews the livestream and decides if additional support or action is needed.
  • Approach Alert: When active on Axon Fleet 3, Guardian can detect if the door of a stopped vehicle opens and alert the officer through the in-car display and their body-worn camera.

Combined, Axon Body 5 and the expanding AI Era portfolio demonstrate the importance of AI as a critical resource to assist public safety professionals before, during and after an incident — reducing administrative burden, improving situational awareness and helping protect more lives.

Innovating Responsibly

Axon's Responsible Innovation framework guides the development of all of its products. Designed with this in mind, Axon Body 5 and Guardian prioritize human oversight and maintain agency control over data. As a key part of the responsible innovation process, Axon's independent Ethics and Equity Advisory Council was created to help responsibly develop and deploy new technologies with transparency, while aligning with community expectations.

General availability dates for Axon Body 5 and Axon Guardian will be announced soon. Product features and capabilities vary by configuration. For more information on Axon's current products and services: Axon Product Catalog - Axon.com.

About AxonAxon (Nasdaq: AXON) is the global leader in public safety technology supporting state, local, federal and international public safety agencies with technology designed to Protect Life. Complementing its mission, Axon's growing Enterprise market focuses on protecting critical infrastructure and frontline workers across multiple industries including corporate security, hospitality, retail and healthcare. Founder-led since 1993, Axon builds products with transparency and responsibility. From TASER energy devices to today's connected network of hardware - including cameras, drones, and robotics - cloud software, sensors, and AI-tools, the Axon ecosystem helps seamlessly protect people and places when it matters most. To ensure these technologies align with community expectations, Axon's independent Ethics & Equity Advisory Council guides the ethical, inclusive, and accountable design of its products and services. Learn more about the EEAC and Axon's Responsible Innovation framework at Axon Responsibility.

data.title: MF Davids give Goliaths a run for their money
data.description:
In India’s over ₹87-lakh crore mutual fund industry, some of the smallest Davids are giving the biggest Goliaths an uncomfortable lesson in investment performance.

Not through superior distribution networks or decades of experience, but through equity portfolios that have weathered recent market volatility better. The finding revives an awkward question for the industry’s giants: Can success itself become an investment handicap?

Veteran investor Jeremy Grantham once observed: “Size of assets under management is the ultimate barrier to successful investing. As assets grow, you are forced either to pick increasing numbers of decreasingly good stocks or to buy larger, indigestible positions of your original holdings.”

Grantham’s warning has acquired fresh relevance in India’s mutual fund landscape, where the biggest players have accumulated everything newcomers envy — except, in some recent comparisons, the better returns.

A bl.portfolio performance comparison of active equity schemes from newer AMCs that began operations in 2023 or later, against the average performance of the three largest schemes from established AMCs across eight equity fund categories, shows that the newer AMC schemes delivered better average one-year returns, where data was available. The analysis covered 24 active equity schemes across eight newer AMCs.

Return gap

The small-cap battlefield produced the biggest upset. Bajaj Finserv Small Cap returned 7.5 per cent over one year against a negative 2.6 per cent average for the three largest competing schemes and a negative 1.9 per cent for the Nifty Smallcap 250 TRI. Its one-year SIP return stood at 12.3 per cent.

Old Bridge Focused returned 5.4 per cent, while the three largest focused funds averaged a negative 3.5 per cent. The Nifty 500 TRI declined 7.8 per cent. Bajaj Finserv Multi Cap delivered 0.9 per cent, compared with a negative 7.6 per cent average for the largest rivals. Helios Mid Cap lost just 0.6 per cent, against a 3.4 per cent decline among the three largest mid-cap schemes.

Unifi Flexi Cap delivered a 4.6 per cent 1-year SIP return, well ahead of the negative 7.6 per cent category average and negative 8.9 per cent benchmark.

The advantage was less pronounced in categories where portfolios typically have substantial large-cap exposure. Bajaj Finserv Large Cap returned a negative 6.9 per cent, against negative 9.5 per cent for the three largest competitors.

The pattern extended to systematic investments. Across all eight categories, newer schemes delivered better one-year SIP returns than the three largest rivals, reinforcing the breadth of their recent outperformance.

These comparisons are with the largest schemes, not the entire universe of established funds. Several categories also have only one eligible newcomer.

Changing landscape

For decades, India’s mutual fund industry was dominated by established banks, financial institutions and investment houses. Their extensive distribution networks, long operating histories and growing assets helped entrench their market positions.

The established order began facing fresh challengers in July 2023, when Bajaj Finserv Mutual Fund entered the fray, followed by Helios MF, Zerodha MF and Old Bridge MF. Another wave, including Unifi MF, Jio BlackRock MF and Capitalmind MF, arrived in 2025. By September 2026, Bajaj Finserv and Helios had each amassed more than ₹8,500 crore in assets, signalling the growing scale of the newcomers.

Smaller portfolios can move into less-liquid stocks without significantly affecting prices.

For larger funds, even a promising investment can pose a logistical challenge: deploying substantial capital without moving the market is no easy task.

Portfolio disclosures offer glimpses of this flexibility. Unifi Flexi Cap increased its allocation to South Indian Bank from 2.2 per cent to 4.7 per cent, while the stock gained 35 per cent over six months. Bajaj Finserv Small Cap raised its exposure to Welspun Corp, whose stock gained nearly 99 per cent.

Several newer schemes also held stocks in the capital markets, industrials and manufacturing sectors. However, changes in portfolio weights do not necessarily indicate fresh buying or successful market timing; price appreciation alone can increase a stock’s share of a portfolio. Not every David has found its slingshot, though. The Wealth Company Flexi Cap Fund lost 9.7 per cent over one year, underscoring that a relatively young fund is no guarantee of investment success.

There are other caveats. The performance window remains short, and two-year track records are unavailable for several schemes. Differences in sector exposure, cash holdings and investment styles can also explain variations in returns. It is too early to draw firm conclusions, and investors will need to assess whether the outperformance persists across longer market cycles.

Scale, experience and an established franchise can confer formidable advantages and remain important considerations when choosing a fund. But they do not automatically translate into superior returns. For now, the Davids have landed some telling blows. The Goliaths may yet have the last laugh, but their sheer size no longer looks quite so intimidating.

data.title: Argentine judge clears Milei and 10 others in LIBRA case, finding no ‘criminally relevant deception’
data.description:
An Argentine federal judge on Friday dismissed the criminal case against President Javier Milei over his promotion of the LIBRA token, ruling that the events under investigation "do not fit any legal offense" for Milei and 10 others.

Judge Marcelo Martínez de Giorgi's 60-page ruling clears Milei, his sister Karina Milei, who is the presidency's secretary general, and nine others. Among them are Hayden Davis, the American who described himself as LIBRA's "launch adviser," crypto lobbyist Mauricio Novelli, and Julian Peh of KIP Protocol.

The ruling follows prosecutor Eduardo Taiano's request for the dismissal of the case. None of the 11 people investigated was called to give a formal statement as a suspect in the case.

Milei posted about LIBRA on X on the evening of Feb. 14, 2025, before the token spiked in value, then deleted the post following the token's sudden crash. Milei later said he had acted in good faith. The token's market cap topped $4.5 billion before falling about 95% mere hours after the token's rise, and eight wallets tied to the team cashed out $107 million, according to onchain analysts.

Judge finds no 'criminally relevant deception'

The judge sided with the prosecutor, Taiano, finding that the evidence did not establish "criminally relevant deception" by Milei or his co-defendants. Milei's office "could have conferred particular repercussion and visibility" on the token, he wrote in Spanish. But the notoriety of whoever promotes an asset and the publicity around a launch "do not, in themselves, amount to a fraudulent scheme," the judge found.

The judge also examined a note recovered from Novelli's phone that, according to El Destape's reporting in March, described three payments totaling $5 million. Forensic analysis confirmed that the note had existed in Apple Notes but could not establish that it had been sent to Davis or anyone else, the judge wrote. Investigators also found deleted chats with a contact saved as "Karina Milei RRPP" and records of calls between Milei and Novelli but could not determine their content.

On Karina Milei, the judge found that the only paper trail linking her to Davis was the presidency's record of her authorizing his entry to the Casa Rosada, the Argentine president's seat of government, on July 16, 2024. That authorization, "considered in isolation, does not demonstrate the existence of an illicit agreement," the judge wrote. Separately, he cited an internal disciplinary investigation that found an employee of DATIP, the prosecutors' forensic unit, had improperly accessed reserved case files, some of which leaked to the press.

Milei cheers while opposition alleges a cover-up

Milei cheered the dismissal of the case with an X post on Friday evening. "Justice has once again put things in their place, exposing the TREMENDOUS political and media operation whose sole aim was to damage the presidential office for coup-mongering political ends," Milei wrote.

Maximiliano Ferraro, the opposition deputy who chaired Congress' LIBRA investigative commission, responded to the ruling with a video posted to X. "We are facing a clear planned judicial operation of cover-up and impunity for Milei and all the organizers of the scam," Ferraro wrote in Spanish.

"They never explained, nor were they ever required to explain, the dozens of meetings that $LIBRA's promoters held at the Casa Rosada and the Quinta de Olivos, the cryptocurrency transactions before and after meeting with the president of the nation, and the calls by Milei ... on the day of the scam," Ferraro said in the video.

The Ferraro-led commission's report, released in November 2025, found that Milei had provided "essential collaboration" to the project. Judge Martínez de Giorgi's ruling does not mention it.

Plaintiffs seek path to appeal

Taiano is not expected to appeal the ruling, per Perfil, and no private plaintiffs remain in the case. In July, at the request of Novelli's lawyers, Martínez de Giorgi removed five investors who had joined as plaintiffs from the case. Appeals judges Mariano Llorens and Pablo Bertuzzi upheld that on Sept. 4, writing that LIBRA buyers "voluntarily assumed the risks inherent in that type of purchase."

The investors have since gone to the Federal Criminal Cassation Court, according to La Política Online, asking to be added back to the case. If that court reinstates them, they could appeal Friday's dismissal.

On July 15, 12 days after the plaintiffs were removed, Milei and Justice Minister Juan Bautista Mahiques signed a decree naming Martínez de Giorgi's wife, Ana María Cristina Juan, to a federal court, Infobae reported. The Senate had approved Juan's nomination before the decree was signed.

Opposition lawmakers, including Unión por la Patria deputy Sabrina Selva, questioned the appointment in their criticisms of Friday's ruling, per Ámbito.

The Block has reached out to the Office of the President and to representatives for Davis for comment.

data.title: Castrol India Q3 profit falls 22.6% as raw-material costs surge 71%
data.description:
Castrol India’s net profit fell 22.6 per cent to ₹176.37 crore in July–September 2026 from ₹227.80 crore in July–September 2025, as rising raw-material costs and adverse currency movements squeezed earnings ahead of a proposed change in the company’s ultimate ownership.

Revenue from operations rose 27.3 per cent to ₹1,734.72 crore from ₹1,362.75 crore, while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) declined 18.8 per cent to ₹262.04 crore from ₹322.80 crore, according to third-quarter results announced on Saturday. Castrol follows a January–December financial year.

“In a quarter marked by a sharp rise in raw material costs and adverse currency movements, Castrol delivered a resilient performance,” Managing Director Saugata Basuray said in the earnings release.

“Pricing actions taken early in the year helped moderate the impact on margins,” he added.

The deterioration follows management’s warning during its August Q2 earnings call that lower-cost inventory had cushioned profitability and commodity inflation would become more visible in September.

“As communicated in August, we expect the operating environment to remain volatile and inflationary,” Chief Financial Officer Mrinalini Srinivasan said.

“We will act with agility to manage margin pressures through pricing and cost actions, while remaining focused on growing market share across every segment in which we operate,” she added.

Ownership transition

The results come as BP prepares to sell a 65 per cent controlling stake in its global Castrol lubricants business to investment firm Stonepeak, in a transaction valuing the business at approximately $10 billion. The deal would give Stonepeak indirect control of Castrol India, in which UK-based Castrol Limited holds 51 per cent.

The proposed change in control has led to a mandatory open-offer process for Indian shareholders. Stonepeak and its partners have proposed acquiring up to 26 per cent of Castrol India’s shares at an initial price of ₹194.04 apiece, representing a potential outlay of approximately ₹4,990 crore.

Castrol India would remain listed unless a separate delisting process is undertaken. Its existing operations are not automatically affected by the proposed ownership change, which remains subject to regulatory approvals. Completion of the global transaction is targeted by the end of 2026.

Margins under pressure

Raw and packing material consumption surged 70.8 per cent to ₹1,085.86 crore from ₹635.79 crore, lifting material costs to 62.6 per cent of revenue from 46.7 per cent a year earlier.

The EBITDA margin contracted to 15.1 per cent from 23.7 per cent, a decline of approximately 860 basis points. Total expenses increased 41 per cent to ₹1,504.74 crore from ₹1,067.18 crore, outpacing revenue growth.

For January–September 2026, net profit stood at ₹766.25 crore, up 8.6 per cent from ₹705.26 crore a year earlier. Revenue grew 20.3 per cent to ₹5,151.43 crore from ₹4,281.58 crore, while EBITDA increased 11 per cent to ₹1,086 crore.

data.title: Setco Automotive swings to ₹203.61 crore profit, plans Lava Cast merger to cut costs
data.description:
Setco Automotive, a Tier-1 component manufacturer historically known for supplying heavy-duty clutches to commercial vehicle makers including Tata Motors, Ashok Leyland and BharatBenz, reported a sharp turnaround in its April–June 2026 earnings, which were approved by its board on October 23, nearly four months after the quarter ended. The results, released after the July–September quarter had already closed, coincided with the company’s decision to merge its loss-making casting subsidiary, Lava Cast, into the listed entity to reduce costs and streamline operations.

Consolidated net profit attributable to shareholders swung from a loss of ₹34.92 crore in April–June 2025 to a profit of ₹203.61 crore in April–June 2026, a positive swing of ₹238.53 crore, largely driven by an investment gain.

Consolidated revenue from operations increased from ₹47.12 crore to ₹52.90 crore over the same period, a year-on-year increase of 12.3%.

Lava Cast merger targets cost savings

Setco’s board approved the revised merger proposal on October 23, under which wholly owned Lava Cast, a manufacturer of casting components for commercial and passenger vehicles, would be absorbed into the listed company.

Lava Cast recorded turnover of ₹87.78 crore in FY26 and negative net worth of ₹136.71 crore as of March 31, 2026.

The merger aims to eliminate overlapping management functions and reduce accounting, auditing, compliance and tax-filing requirements, delivering what Setco describes as a “consequential reduction in administrative costs”. The company has not quantified the expected savings.

The restructuring follows Setco’s phased divestment of its clutch manufacturing subsidiary, Setco Auto Systems, to RSB Transmissions.

The first closing on May 27, 2026, involved the sale of approximately 41% of the subsidiary for around ₹215 crore, leaving Setco with a residual stake of approximately 24%.

The agreements also provide for a ₹33-crore capacity-reservation fee payable to Lava Cast, linking the retained casting operations with the divested clutch business.

Since Lava Cast is already consolidated, its absorption would not independently increase group revenue or eliminate accumulated losses. No cash consideration or fresh shares are involved.

Standalone profit boosted by investment gain

Standalone net profit increased from ₹0.99 crore to ₹205.30 crore, an increase of approximately 20,637%, while revenue from operations declined from ₹0.38 crore to nil.

Other income included a ₹214.28-crore investment gain and ₹2.25 crore in non-compete income, indicating that the earnings surge was driven principally by non-operating income.

Costs outpace revenue.

Consolidated material costs increased from ₹20.12 crore to ₹27.95 crore, a year-on-year increase of 38.9%, while employee expenses rose from ₹10.58 crore to ₹19.49 crore, an increase of 84.2%. Finance costs declined from ₹2.34 crore to ₹1.82 crore, a decrease of 22.2%.

Lava Cast’s quarterly loss narrowed from ₹4.40 crore to ₹2.35 crore, a reduction of 46.6%, although its negative net worth widened from ₹107.02 crore in June 2025 to ₹139.06 crore in June 2026.

Auditors flag financial risks

Auditors highlighted material uncertainty over Lava Cast’s ability to continue as a going concern and qualified Setco’s consolidated financial review because four overseas entities were included using management-certified financial information without audit or limited review.

The merger remains subject to regulatory and tribunal approvals, with its financial benefits dependent on actual cost reductions and improved operating performance.

data.title: Wall Street Assets Take Nearly A Quarter Of Crypto Perpetual Trading: Glassnode Report
data.description:
Key points:
  • Perpetual futures on stocks, ETFs, indices, gold and oil grew to 23.5% of perpetual volume on major crypto exchanges.
  • About $778 billion of these contracts traded in August, with Binance handling about 55% of the volume.
  • On Hyperliquid, markets tied to traditional assets now trade 85% as much as the venue's own Bitcoin contract.

Bitcoin (BTC) fell to $80,000 on Saturday as traditional financial assets including stocks, ETFs, indices, gold and oil are capturing a larger share of trading activity on crypto exchanges. Perpetual futures tied to these assets made up 23.5% of volume in August, up from just 0.5% in November of last year, according to a report by Glassnode and Fasanara Digital.

Traditional Asset Perpetuals Hit $778B

Perpetual futures are derivatives with no expiry date, which allow traders to hold leveraged positions for as long as they like. The share of these contracts tied to traditional assets rose from 0.5% of volume on six major exchange groups in November 2025 to 23.5% in August 2026, the report said. About $778 billion worth changed hands in August alone, up from $23.5 billion in November.

Trading in crypto-asset perpetuals fell 49% over the same period, which also lifted the traditional-asset share. Even if crypto volume had stayed at its November level, the share would still have reached 13.5% in August, the report said. The firms noted that their figures are conservative. Contracts they could not classify were counted as crypto.

Bitcoin was the top-trending ticker on Stocktwits. Bitcoin’s price was down over 2% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

Binance Takes The Lead

Binance (BNB) did not list its first such contract until December 2025. By August, it handled about 55% of the volume, or $429 billion. OKX came second with a little over 15%, followed by Hyperliquid (HYPE) at 11%. Traditional assets made up a larger part of the business on Hyperliquid, as they accounted for 35.2% of all perpetual volume on the platform in August, against 27.6% on Binance.

Hyperliquid’s (HYPE) HIP-3 system, live since October 2025, allows users to create perpetual markets for any asset that has a reliable price source.

Markets listed on trade.xyz, an exchange built on that system, now trade 85% as much volume as Hyperliquid’s own Bitcoin perpetual, up from less than a tenth at the start of the year, the report said. At the start of the year, it was below a tenth. The same types of contracts topped the rankings on every platform. These included memory-chip stocks, leveraged chip and Korea-focused ETFs, and commodities such as gold, silver and crude oil.

Bitcoin Moves With Gold

The report also tracked Bitcoin's behavior around the U.S. Treasury's decision to raise the maximum size of its long-dated bond buybacks from $2 billion to at least $4 billion. Bitcoin rose 25% that week, while gold climbed and stocks slipped. Since then, Bitcoin has traded more like gold. Their correlation peaked on September 11 at its highest level since the data began in March 2018, according to the report.

data.title: Capital Research Raises Metaplanet Voting Stake To 11.11%
data.description:
TL;DR: Capital Research and Management’s reported Metaplanet voting stake reached 11.11% as of October 16. Both a larger holding and a share buyback affected the percentage.

Metaplanet has disclosed that Capital Research and Management crossed the 10% voting-rights threshold, based on an investor report.

The company’s October 23 notice puts the investment adviser’s reported position at 143,301,084 shares as of October 16, equivalent to 11.11% of voting rights. The September 8 comparison showed 125,455,820 shares and a 9.32% stake.

The two snapshots show 17,845,264 additional reported shares. That arithmetic does not date individual trades or establish a new corporate Bitcoin purchase.

Both Sides Of The Ownership Calculation Changed

The percentage also reflects treasury shares acquired in Metaplanet’s October 14 buyback, which reduced the voting-rights denominator.

Ownership percentages are fractions: the investor’s holding sits above the total carrying voting rights. Increasing the first figure or reducing the second makes the percentage larger, so comparing the percentages alone can obscure what happened.

Voting power also answers a narrower question than economic exposure: how much influence accompanies a holding. Share classes, treasury stock and financing claims can make a simple percentage a poor substitute for analysing the investment.

Metaplanet relied on the investor’s October 23 change report and said it had not independently confirmed beneficial ownership.

The Buyback Puts Share Count In Focus

In a separate October 14 announcement, Metaplanet disclosed the completed repurchase of 73,981,400 ordinary shares at ¥261 each, costing ¥19.309 billion. The transaction used the Tokyo Stock Exchange’s ToSTNeT-3 off-auction repurchase system.

The broader authorisation permits up to 200 million ordinary shares and ¥60 billion of purchases between October 14, 2026 and October 13, 2027. Those are programme ceilings, not an assertion that the entire amount has already been spent.

The company linked its repurchase policy to capital efficiency and Bitcoin holdings per share. That framing is significant for treasury-company investors because the number of shares participates directly in their economic exposure to corporate assets.

A shrinking share count can increase an asset-per-share measure even when the underlying asset balance stays unchanged. Conversely, raising capital through new shares can expand the balance sheet while changing each existing share’s claim on it. Neither calculation alone establishes whether a transaction creates value after its financing costs.

There is also a distinction between a listed equity and personal coin ownership. Holding shares on an exchange introduces corporate financing, governance and management decisions alongside exposure to a company’s Bitcoin strategy. Direct custody of coins has a different set of responsibilities.

For shareholders assessing that strategy, the useful comparison therefore extends beyond total coins held. It includes the shares sharing those assets, obligations against the balance sheet and the price paid to obtain the exposure.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: The Rare-Earth Vultures Harvesting Metals From America's Old Wind Turbines — WSJ
data.description:
By Ed Ballard | Photography and video by KC McGinnis for WSJ

To MidAmerican Energy, the wind turbines being taken down and dismantled at its Highland wind farm in O'Brien County, Iowa, are junk. To Brian Diesselhorst, they are the mother lode.

Diesselhorst is chief executive of Paladin EnviroTech, a recycling company eyeing a new role as a supplier of rare-earth metals. The U.S. is trying to reduce its reliance on China for rare earths, which go into everything from drones to MRI scanners. Paladin is among a few ventures betting that the quickest route to new supply goes through the junkyard.

Rare-earth metals with names like dysprosium and neodymium are used in magnets that go into electric motors. Diesselhorst is in the market for various expired gadgets. But retired wind turbines, whose room-size generators in some cases house huge rare-earth magnets, are his No. 1 target. Some more recent models can contain nearly a ton of rare earths, worth close to $100,000, Paladin estimates.

There are thousands of retirement-age turbines waiting to be harvested as America's wind industry ages. Only a fraction of the earlier models contain rare earths — 20% of the turbines being replaced at the Highland facility have them — but they became commonplace in more-powerful turbines. Those are now starting to be replaced, so this source of waste is gradually becoming more valuable.

"That's why it was critical for us to get into the game now," said Diesselhorst, who says he believes Paladin is the first company to start harvesting this source of rare earths.

China established its rare-earth dominance over decades by providing financial support for domestic companies and flooding the market to squash nascent competitors. Last year, with the trade war with the U.S. heating up, Beijing flexed its muscles by imposing export restrictions that laid bare Western manufacturers' dependency on China.

Recycling ventures are one part of a drive to loosen that chokehold. The Trump administration is providing billions of dollars for mineral ventures, but the investments will take years to pay off.

For the most part, the old turbines being taken out of service are replaced with better ones. Those at the Highland wind farm have been spinning for a decade and could serve another decade, according to Adam Jablonski, vice president of project development at MidAmerican Energy, the Berkshire Hathaway-owned utility that owns the site.

But replacing them with better models, with blades 20% longer, will let each supply about 15% more power, Jablonski said — a boon when electricity demand is rising and developing new energy projects is slow and expensive.

MidAmerican has turned two things the Midwest has in abundance — wind and space — into the largest wind-power business of any U.S. utility. It has already replaced nearly 1,500 of its 3,700 turbines. Metal recyclers harvested what they could, but until Paladin came along the rare-earth metals that some of them contained were going to waste.

A barrier to entry is the cumbersome task of dismantling turbines. Cranes have to remove the blades and the nacelles — the room-size housings that contain the turbine generators. Then the components are sliced up with hydraulic shears and other equipment and loaded onto heavy-duty trucks.

"You're dealing with 80-to-120,000-pound pieces that you've got to load on flatbeds," said Luke Wray, the Paladin executive charged with overseeing the company's supplies of rare earths and other critical minerals. "You're on a field in the middle of nowhere. If you've got mud, or you're on clay, and the groundsoil isn't sturdy, you could have a crane tip over."

On one job, when contractors were using explosives to fell turbines, hubs weighing more than 30 tons ended up buried deep in clay and had to be arduously excavated. Another risk comes from the wind itself — strong gusts can play havoc with blades being moved by cranes.

The other deterrent is the challenge of separating materials cost-effectively so the sought-after rare earths can be isolated, ground up and turned into metal for new magnets. Paladin works with Critical Materials Recycling, a Boone, Iowa company that is commercializing a leaching process developed at Ames National Laboratory to extract nearly all the rare earths from electronic waste.

Recyclers primarily targeted copper. Turbines contain several tons of copper in their wiring and other components, with a ton worth roughly $14,500 at today's prices.

Rare earths, harder to separate and less valuable, are generally recycled alongside steel and end up irretrievably lost in a byproduct called slag.

Several U.S. battery-recycling ventures ran into trouble in recent years in part because they couldn't source enough feedstock and bring costs down.

Diesselhorst is counting on securing enough turbines to run the recycling operation efficiently. Next year, Paladin forecasts, wind-turbine magnets will account for roughly 40% of its tonnage, with MRI machines and EV motors contributing about 25% each and hard drives accounting for the last 10%.

Wray has lined up a pipeline of about 500 turbines across the U.S. In the company's Tampa, Fla., offices, a poster of Don Quixote, the fictional knight who tilted at windmills, hangs on the wall, with a smaller portrait of Wray in the corner.

data.title: IT stocks Q2 results analysis: Infosys vs TCS vs Wipro vs HCL vs TechM: Who wins profit, revenue, dividend, AI race?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- India's largest IT companies are showing signs of recovery, with most delivering stronger profits and deal bookings while some struggle with sluggish client spending and pressure on revenue growth.

The September quarter (Q2FY27) results of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech and Tech Mahindra reveal a widening gap in performance, particularly in constant-currency growth, artificial intelligence (AI) monetisation and future revenue visibility.

While Tech Mahindra led profit and revenue growth, HCLTech stood out for raising its growth guidance, Infosys announced the highest interim dividend, and TCS retained its lead in deal bookings and AI revenue scale. Wipro, meanwhile, faced pressure on profitability and new business wins.

Net profit: Tech Mahindra emerged as the strongest performer in year-on-year profit growth, with net profit surging 32.7% to Rs.1,586 crore. HCLTech followed with a 21.2% increase to Rs.5,132 crore, its highest-ever quarterly net income. TCS reported a 15% rise to Rs.13,884 crore, while Infosys posted a more modest 6% increase to Rs.7,823 crore. However, Wipro's consolidated net profit declined 1.4% to Rs.3,200.6 crore, making it the only company among the four to report a year-on-year profit decline.

Revenue growth: Tech Mahindra also led year-on-year revenue growth, with consolidated revenue increasing 15.6% to Rs.16,180 crore. HCLTech recorded an 11.52% rise to Rs.35,620 crore, narrowly ahead of Infosys, which reported an 11% increase to Rs.49,244 crore. Meanwhile, TCS revenue grew 11.2% to Rs.73,188 crore, the highest in absolute terms among the five companies. Wipro's gross revenue rose 9.1% to Rs.24,752.7 crore, although its core IT services business continued to experience muted growth.

Constant-currency revenue: Tech Mahindra led the reported constant-currency performance, with growth of 7.2% year-on-year and 2.4% quarter-on-quarter. HCLTech followed with 2.3% sequential growth, while Infosys reported 1.2% sequential growth. TCS recorded a more subdued 0.5% quarter-on-quarter increase, whereas Wipro's constant-currency revenue growth stood at just 0.6% year-on-year, highlighting continued weakness in underlying client demand.

AI revenue: TCS led in AI revenue scale, reporting an annualised AI revenue run rate exceeding $3.1 billion, with AI contributing more than 10% of its revenue. Infosys said AI accounted for 10.5% of total revenue, growing 29% sequentially. HCLTech reported $219 million in advanced AI revenue, representing nearly 6% of total revenue and 78% year-on-year constant-currency growth. Wipro did not disclose a standalone AI revenue figure.

Deal wins: TCS secured the largest total contract value (TCV) of $9.6 billion, providing substantial forward revenue visibility despite falling short of internal expectations. Infosys won large deals worth $5.2 billion, including a mega deal exceeding $2 billion, with 62% of the total comprising net new business.

HCLTech recorded $3.26 billion in new bookings, supported by a landmark multi-year deal worth $1.14 billion. Tech Mahindra reported contract wins of $1.02 billion. Wipro's total deal bookings declined to $2.6 billion from $4.7 billion a year earlier, making it the weakest performer on this measure.

Revenue and margin guidance: HCLTech emerged as the most optimistic, raising the lower end of its FY27 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 2.5%-4% from 1%-4%, while retaining its EBIT margin forecast of 17.5%-18.5%. Infosys moved in the opposite direction, cutting its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1%-2% from 1.5%-3%, citing pricing pressure and customers' productivity demands, while maintaining its operating margin outlook at 20%-22%.

Wipro projected sequential constant-currency revenue growth of -1.5% to 0.5% for Q3 FY27. TCS and Tech Mahindra did not provide explicit numerical revenue guidance, although Tech Mahindra reiterated that it remained on track to achieve its 15% EBIT margin target.

Dividends: Infosys announced the highest interim dividend among the five companies at Rs.26 per share. Tech Mahindra declared Rs.15 per share, while TCS and HCLTech each announced an interim dividend of Rs.12 per share. Wipro did not declare an interim dividend for the quarter.

Other corporate actions: Tech Mahindra stood out by approving a 1:1 bonus share issue, subject to board approval. Meanwhile, TCS completed its acquisition of German industrial consulting firm MHP for EUR 320 million to strengthen its automotive capabilities. Wipro expanded its AI portfolio through its 20% stake acquisition in FLARRE.AI.

Overall, Tech Mahindra led profit and revenue growth, TCS dominated deal bookings and AI revenue scale, and HCLTech delivered the strongest improvement in growth guidance. Infosys led on dividend payout, while Wipro faced the greatest pressure across profitability and deal wins.

New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Despite nearly falling 20% in the last 1 month, domestic brokerage house Deven Choksey Research has initiated coverage on Siemens Energy India with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs.4,554, implying a potential upside of 72% from the last closing price of Rs.2,649.

The report said, "We assign multiple of 60x PE on FY28 EPS of 75.90 and arrive at TP of INR 4,554, implying 41% upside on Siemens Energy India Ltd. We have not factored HVDC into our TP, while new HVDC VSC orders and nuclear energy provide additional upside optionality."

The brokerage expects the power equipment maker to benefit from India's multi-year transmission investment cycle, rising electricity demand, renewable energy integration and expansion in high-voltage grid infrastructure.

It highlighted the company's position in high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission, grid-stabilisation solutions, power generation equipment and engineering services. Its strong parentage through Siemens Energy Germany and opportunities in exports could further support growth.

Deven Choksey Research said, "We view Siemens Energy India as a high-potential play on the country's power transmission and generation opportunity, with a diversified business model spanning grid infrastructure, power generation, services and engineering, research & development (ER&D)."

The stock ended 4.4% lower at Rs.2,649 on Friday, October 23. It has been under pressure in recent times. The power stock has declined around 10% in 1 week, nearly 20% in 1 month, and 3 months. Meanwhile, it has lost 15% in the last 1 year.

It hit its 52-week high of Rs.3,966.80 in May 2026 and its 52-week low of Rs.2105.15 in January 2026.

The brokerage's investment thesis centres on rising transmission expenditure as India expands renewable energy capacity and strengthens its electricity grid.

According to the report, the Central Electricity Authority's roadmap for 900 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity implies transmission capital expenditure of around Rs.7.93 lakh crore between FY26 and FY36. An estimated Rs.5-6 lakh crore of transmission investment over the next five years could provide sustained demand for transformers, switchgear, substations and grid-stabilisation equipment.

Moreover, Siemens Energy India is among three players in the domestic market with HVDC capabilities and has an estimated 30% share of the segment. The report expects India's voltage-source converter HVDC (VSC-HVDC) market to grow at 15-18% annually through 2030. The company also has more than 50% market share in India's STATCOM segment, which supports grid stability as renewable power generation increases.

The generation business offers additional opportunities. The company has an estimated 55% market share in steam turbines and around 25% of India's gas-turbine fleet. Deven Choksey Research also highlighted the company's manufacturing expansion and export opportunities. Siemens Energy India plans to increase transformer capacity from 15 GVA to 60 GVA by 2030-32, strengthening its ability to serve domestic transmission projects and international markets.

The brokerage said, "We believe Siemens Energy India offers a differentiated combination of structural domestic power-sector growth, exposure to higher-value transmission technologies, recurring generation services, increasing export opportunities and strong global parentage."

Deven Choksey Research expects Siemens Energy India to deliver revenue, EBITDA and profit after tax (PAT) compound annual growth rates (CAGRs) of 25%, 33% and 35%, respectively, over the next three years. The brokerage expects revenue to rise from Rs.78,267 million in FY26 estimates to Rs.1,54,529 million in FY28 estimates, driven by order inflows across power transmission and generation.

The order book stood at Rs.193 billion as of Q3FY26 and is projected to increase to Rs.271 billion by FY28, implying a CAGR of around 19%. The existing order book provides approximately twice the revenue visibility, according to the report.

For valuation, Deven Choksey Research has applied a price-to-earnings multiple of 60 times to its FY28 earnings per share estimate of Rs.75.90 to arrive at the target price of Rs.4,554. The brokerage noted that the stock was trading at around 43 times FY28 estimated earnings, compared with approximately 60 times for peers.

However, the brokerage cautioned that commodity price volatility, currency fluctuations, delays in transmission expenditure, project execution risks, working-capital requirements and competitive pricing pressure could affect growth and profitability.
